title: Cluster 03 DRILL: Energetics in Practice
subtitle: H2 Biology 9477 · Book 5 · 10 questions · 90 marks · 42 parts · the practical cluster, worth roughly twelve percentage points of the whole A-level · every question is an actual exam paper question
intro_html:
Answers sit directly under each part, hidden. Click Show answer only after you have said your full reasoning aloud for that part. Check (a) before you start (b), that is the point of the layout.

Rate your confidence before every reveal. A dashed line sits above each answer block. Say high, medium or guessed out loud before you click.

Read this first, because it reorders your revision plan. Book 5 supplied 60% of the 9477 specimen practical paper, 30 of its 50 marks. Specimen Paper 4 Question 1 is 20 marks on light intensity and the rate of photosynthesis, with pondweed, a syringe and five neutral-density filters. Specimen Paper 4 Question 3 is a 10-mark plan for a compensation-point investigation with hydrogencarbonate indicator and sun and shade ivy leaves. Paper 4 is 20% of the A-level, which makes this cluster roughly twelve percentage points of your final grade on its own, and you have skipped practicals entirely. Questions 1 and 2 below are those two specimen questions.

This is the one cluster where data-led questions are the right kind of question. Clusters 1 and 2 deliberately cut read-off-the-graph items, because a figure there is stimulus for an explain question. Here, reading a table, designing a table, calculating a rate and quoting values with units is the outcome. 36.9% of the whole Book 5 question bank sits under a practical-skills heading, and in the Photosynthesis file alone it is 44.8%.

Two holes in your notes, both filled here from real papers. Your chapter defines the respiratory quotient and derives both calculation cases correctly, then stops without giving the values by substrate. Question 8(d) supplies that missing table, printed inside NYJC's own 2025 Paper 3 stem. Your chapter mentions chromatography once, inside a history box, and never teaches pigment separation at all. Question 6 is your own school's 2023 Paper 4 chromatography chain, mark scheme, layout rule and marker's notes included.

Two MCQs. Q3(d) is a sun-and-shade compensation-point item. Q5(a) is your own school's DCPIP question, on which three quarters of the cohort chose the wrong option because they forgot the chloroplasts are still in the tube. The paper awards one mark for the letter; the drill then makes you justify every statement.

Two real figures, both lifted from the specimen paper PDF. Where a figure could not be recovered, the paper's own prose description is printed and the part is answerable from that description.

Cumulative over Clusters 1 and 2 and over Books 1 to 4. Q1(a) and Q3 need the limiting-factor curve cold. Q4(d) needs the whole feedback chain from carbon dioxide supply back to photolysis. Q5 needs non-cyclic photophosphorylation and where NADP sits in it. Q7(f) needs enzyme kinetics and denaturation from Book 1. Q9(d) needs reducing against non-reducing sugars from Book 1 carbohydrates.

What the marks reward on Paper 4. Three separate examiner comments name the same four failures: selecting the wrong data series, omitting units, not reading to half the smallest division, and not noticing the graph does not start at the origin. The habit that beats all four is fixed: describe the trend, quote two values with units from the correct series, then account for it. In a table, units go in the heading only and the independent variable goes in the leftmost column. In a plan, answer the printed bullet list in the order it is printed, because that is what the marks are attached to.

How to run it. Questions 1 and 2 are 26 marks between them and are best run in one sitting on their own.

One primary concept each, checked for duplicated required answers and not merely for duplicated labels. Q1 the whole 20-mark specimen practical, predict to improve · Q2 the 10-mark compensation-point plan · Q3 compensation point read off a net-exchange curve · Q4 what a gas measurement in green tissue actually measures · Q5 the redox dye that isolates the light-dependent reaction, and the endpoint three quarters got wrong · Q6 chromatography and Rf, the node your notes never teach · Q7 the respirometer and what the absorbent is for · Q8 respiratory quotient, the other node your notes never finish · Q9 yeast, and the three factors LO 3(k) names · Q10 data-quoting discipline as a skill in its own right. One question is deliberately moved in from another cluster. Q10(a) is 9477 Specimen Paper 2 Question 5(c), which belongs to the Calvin cycle by content but is a data-handling item by skill, so it sits here rather than in the Cluster 1 drill, where the rest of Specimen Q5 lives.

Nothing from Books 6 to 9. The biology of the light-dependent reactions, the Calvin cycle, glycolysis, the link reaction, the Krebs cycle and oxidative phosphorylation belongs to Clusters 1 and 2; here it is only ever the reason a reading moves. Leaf anatomy, mesophyll and stomata carry no learning outcome as Paper 2 recall but stay alive as Paper 4 material, which is why sun and shade leaves are described in that vocabulary in Question 2.
